records.source: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מְגוּרֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And dwelt Jacob in [the] land of [the] sojournings of his father, in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: Jacob stayed on in the land where his father had lived as a foreigner, the land of Canaan.

L.1: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

R.1: Jacob lived in Canaan, the land where his father Isaac had lived as a foreigner.

decisions.choice: his father's sojournings: where Isaac lived as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The word means living in a land as an outsider without owning it. Esau has just settled in Seir (36:8); Jacob stays in the promised land, still as a guest in it, as Abraham and Isaac were (17:8; Hebrews 11:9).

decisions.choice: his father Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable names the father for clarity.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה׀תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־דִּבָּתָ֥ם רָעָ֖ה אֶל־אֲבִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: These [are the] generations of Jacob. Joseph, a son of seventeen year[s], was shepherding with his brothers in the flock; and he [was] a youth with [the] sons of Bilhah and with [the] sons of Zilpah, [the] wives of his father; and brought Joseph their report, bad, to their father.
pieces: This is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was seventeen, he used to tend the flocks with his brothers, working as a helper alongside the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, two of his father's wives. Joseph brought their father an unfavorable report about them.

L.2: These [are] the generations of Jacob. Joseph, [being] seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers. He [was] a young man with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.

R.2: Here is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he took care of the sheep and goats with his brothers. He worked with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, who were wives of his father. Joseph told his father bad things about what his brothers were doing.

decisions.choice: the generations of Jacob: the heading of the story of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: This heading (toledot) opens each major section of Genesis (2:4; 6:9; 11:27; 25:19). What follows is less a list of names than the story of Jacob's family, centered on Joseph and Judah, to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: a youth with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah: a junior helper
decisions.reason: Na'ar means a young man, and often a young helper or attendant. Joseph works under the sons of the two slave wives.

decisions.choice: a bad report of them: an unfavorable account, perhaps slander
decisions.reason: The phrase (dibbah ra'ah) can mean an accurate but damaging report or a malicious one (Numbers 13:32). The narrator does not say whether Joseph's report was true.

records.source: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִכָּל־בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי־בֶן־זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ כְּתֹ֥נֶת פַּסִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, for a son of old age [was] he to him; and he made for him a tunic of palms.
pieces: Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, since he had been born to him in his old age, and he had a long-sleeved robe made for him.

L.3: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he [was] the son of his old age; and he made him a tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles].

R.3: Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because Joseph was born when Israel was old. Israel gave Joseph a special robe with long sleeves.

decisions.choice: a tunic of passim: a long robe reaching to the wrists and ankles
decisions.reason: Passim probably means "palms (of the hands) and soles (of the feet)": a full-length robe with long sleeves, not the short working tunic of a shepherd. The ancient Greek translation took it as "many-colored", the source of the familiar "coat of many colors". The only other such garment in Scripture is worn by a king's daughter (2 Samuel 13:18-19). Either way it marked Joseph out as favored and exempt from hard work.

decisions.choice: the son of his old age: born late in Jacob's life
decisions.reason: Joseph was the first son of Rachel, Jacob's loved wife, born after long waiting (30:22-24). Benjamin is younger, but Joseph is the son of Jacob's old age in the story's eyes.

decisions.choice: a long-sleeved robe
decisions.reason: The familiar rendering follows the Greek translation; the Hebrew points to the robe's length and sleeves rather than its color.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי־אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכָּל־אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּשְׂנְא֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ דַּבְּר֥וֹ לְשָׁלֹֽם׃
records.gloss: And saw his brothers that him loved their father more than all his brothers, and they hated him and were not able to speak to him for peace.
pieces: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, and they hated him so much that they could not say a friendly word to him.

L.4: And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him and could not speak to him peaceably.

R.4: His brothers could see that their father loved Joseph more than any of them. So they hated Joseph and could not even speak kindly to him.

decisions.choice: speak to him for peace: speak to him in a friendly way
decisions.reason: To speak "for peace" (shalom) is to speak on good terms, and may include the ordinary greeting. The brothers could not manage even that.

records.source: וַיַּחֲלֹ֤ם יוֹסֵף֙ חֲל֔וֹם וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיּוֹסִ֥פוּ ע֖וֹד שְׂנֹ֥א אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And dreamed Joseph a dream and told [it] to his brothers, and they increased again to hate him.
pieces: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, their hatred of him grew worse.

L.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream and told [it] to his brothers, and they hated him still more.

R.5: One night Joseph had a dream. When he told his brothers about it, they hated him even more.

decisions.choice: Joseph dreamed a dream: the first of the dreams that shape his story
decisions.reason: Dreams come in pairs in the Joseph story: two here (verses 5-11), two in prison (40:5), two for Pharaoh (41:1-7). Joseph later says that God gives their meaning (40:8; 41:16).

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֕א הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָלָֽמְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, hear, please, this dream which I have dreamed:
pieces: "Listen to this dream I had," he said to them.

L.6: And he said to them, "Please hear this dream that I have dreamed:

R.6: He said to them, "Listen to the dream I had.

records.source: וְ֠הִנֵּה אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מְאַלְּמִ֤ים אֲלֻמִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה קָ֥מָה אֲלֻמָּתִ֖י וְגַם־נִצָּ֑בָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה תְסֻבֶּ֨ינָה֙ אֲלֻמֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַתִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖יןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And behold, we [were] binding sheaves in [the] middle of the field, and behold, arose my sheaf and also stood upright; and behold, gathered round your sheaves and bowed down to my sheaf.
pieces: "We were out in the field tying up bundles of grain, when all at once my bundle got up and stood on end, and your bundles came around it and bowed low before it."

L.7: Look, we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and look, my sheaf rose and also stood upright; and look, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf."

R.7: We were in the field, tying stalks of grain into bundles. Suddenly my bundle stood up straight. Then your bundles gathered around it and bowed down to my bundle."

decisions.choice: bowed down: the gesture of honor to a superior
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the brothers later bow before Joseph in Egypt (42:6; 43:26; 50:18), where the dream comes true.

decisions.choice: and look ... and look ... and look: the dreamer's vivid telling
decisions.reason: Hinneh, repeated three times, lets the hearers see the dream unfold through the dreamer's eyes.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ אֶחָ֔יו הֲמָלֹ֤ךְ תִּמְלֹךְ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אִם־מָשׁ֥וֹל תִּמְשֹׁ֖ל בָּ֑נוּ וַיּוֹסִ֤פוּ עוֹד֙ שְׂנֹ֣א אֹת֔וֹ עַל־חֲלֹמֹתָ֖יו וְעַל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said to him his brothers, really reign will you reign over us, or really rule will you rule over us? And they increased again to hate him on account of his dreams and on account of his words.
pieces: His brothers answered, "So you think you will be king over us, do you? Are you going to be our master?" And they hated him all the more because of his dreams and the way he told them.

L.8: And his brothers said to him, "Will you indeed reign over us? Or will you indeed rule over us?" And they hated him still more for his dreams and for his words.

R.8: His brothers said to him, "Do you really think you will be our king? Will you really rule over us?" So they hated him even more because of his dreams and what he said.

decisions.choice: will you indeed reign ... indeed rule: scornful emphasis
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis, and the questions are sarcastic. Without knowing it, the brothers name what will happen.

decisions.choice: his words: what he said, the telling of the dreams
decisions.reason: Not only the dreams but Joseph's telling of them angered his brothers.

records.source: וַיַּחֲלֹ֥ם עוֹד֙ חֲל֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה חָלַ֤מְתִּֽי חֲלוֹם֙ ע֔וֹד וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֖ים לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he dreamed again another dream and recounted it to his brothers and said, behold, I have dreamed a dream again, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars [were] bowing down to me.
pieces: Then he had a second dream and told that one to his brothers as well. "Listen," he said, "I have had another dream. This time the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing to me."

L.9: And he dreamed yet another dream and told it to his brothers and said, "Look, I have dreamed another dream: and look, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."

R.9: Later Joseph had another dream, and he told his brothers about it too. He said, "I had another dream. The sun, the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."

decisions.choice: the sun, the moon and eleven stars: his father, his mother and his eleven brothers
decisions.reason: Jacob reads the dream so at once (verse 10). The second dream reaches beyond the field into the sky and includes the parents.

records.source: וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר אֶל־אָבִיו֮ וְאֶל־אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּגְעַר־בּ֣וֹ אָבִ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And he recounted [it] to his father and to his brothers, and rebuked him his father and said to him, what [is] this dream which you have dreamed? Really come will we come, I and your mother and your brothers, to bow down to you to [the] ground?
pieces: When he told it to his father as well as his brothers, his father scolded him. "What sort of dream is this?" he said. "Are your mother and I and your brothers really going to come and bow to the ground in front of you?"

L.10: And he told [it] to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him, "What [is] this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the ground before you?"

R.10: He told the dream to his father and his brothers. But his father scolded him. "What kind of dream is this?" he asked. "Will your mother and I and your brothers really come and bow down to the ground in front of you?"

decisions.choice: your mother: Rachel, though she has died (35:19)
alternatives: Leah, as the mother of the household
a figure for the family as a whole
decisions.reason: Rachel's death has already been told. Jacob may mean the family as a whole, or the dream may simply include her; the text does not explain.

records.source: וַיְקַנְאוּ־ב֖וֹ אֶחָ֑יו וְאָבִ֖יו שָׁמַ֥ר אֶת־הַדָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And were jealous of him his brothers, and his father kept the matter.
pieces: His brothers envied him, but his father did not forget what he had said.

L.11: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter [in mind].

R.11: His brothers were jealous of Joseph. But his father kept thinking about what Joseph had said.

decisions.choice: kept the matter: kept it in mind, waiting to see
decisions.reason: Jacob rebukes Joseph aloud but holds on to the dream, wondering what it means (compare Luke 2:19).

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶחָ֑יו לִרְע֛וֹת אֶׄתׄ־צֹ֥אןאֲבִיהֶ֖ם בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And went his brothers to pasture [the] flock of their father at Shechem.
pieces: One time his brothers had gone to graze their father's flocks near Shechem.

L.12: And his brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.

R.12: Joseph's brothers went to Shechem to find grass for their father's sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: at Shechem: where the brothers had killed the men of the city
decisions.reason: Shechem was about 50 miles (80 km) north of Hebron, and the place of the massacre in chapter 34. Sending Joseph there alone was not without risk.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם לְכָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ הִנֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Israel to Joseph, [are] not your brothers pasturing at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them. And he said to him, here I [am].
pieces: Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are grazing the flocks near Shechem, are they not? Come, I am going to send you to them." "I am ready," Joseph replied.

L.13: And Israel said to Joseph, "Are not your brothers pasturing [the flock] at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them." And he said to him, "Here I am."

R.13: Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are taking care of the sheep and goats near Shechem. I want you to go to them." Joseph answered, "I will go."

decisions.choice: here I am: ready to do what is asked
decisions.reason: The same answer Abraham gives when called (22:1, 11). It expresses readiness to obey.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ־נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת־שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֵ֖נִי דָּבָ֑ר וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֨הוּ֙ מֵעֵ֣מֶק חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א שְׁכֶֽמָה׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, go, please, see [the] welfare of your brothers and [the] welfare of the flock, and bring back to me word. And he sent him from [the] valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
pieces: "Go and find out how your brothers are doing and how the flocks are," he said, "and come back and tell me." So he sent him off from the valley of Hebron, and Joseph made his way to Shechem.

L.14: And he said to him, "Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers and well with the flock, and bring me word." So he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

R.14: Israel said, "Go and see if your brothers and the animals are all right. Then come back and tell me." So Israel sent him from the valley of Hebron, and Joseph went to Shechem.

decisions.choice: the welfare (shalom) of your brothers
decisions.reason: The word shalom echoes verse 4: the brothers could not speak to Joseph with shalom, and now he is sent to see about their shalom.

records.source: וַיִּמְצָאֵ֣הוּ אִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה תֹעֶ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֧הוּ הָאִ֛ישׁ לֵאמֹ֖ר מַה־תְּבַקֵּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And found him a man, and behold, [he was] wandering in the field; and asked him the man, saying, what are you seeking?
pieces: A man came upon him wandering around in the countryside and asked him, "What are you looking for?"

L.15: And a man found him, and look, he was wandering in the open country; and the man asked him, saying, "What are you seeking?"

R.15: A man found Joseph wandering around in the fields. The man asked him, "What are you looking for?"

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־אַחַ֖י אָנֹכִ֣י מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵיפֹ֖ה הֵ֥ם רֹעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said, my brothers I [am] seeking; tell, please, to me where they [are] pasturing.
pieces: "It is my brothers I am trying to find," he answered. "Can you tell me where they are grazing their flocks?"

L.16: And he said, "I am seeking my brothers. Please tell me where they are pasturing [the flock]."

R.16: Joseph answered, "I am looking for my brothers. Can you tell me where they are with their sheep and goats?"

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ נָסְע֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה דֹּתָ֑יְנָה וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יוֹסֵף֙ אַחַ֣ר אֶחָ֔יו וַיִּמְצָאֵ֖ם בְּדֹתָֽן׃
records.gloss: And said the man, they have set out from here, for I heard [them] saying, let us go to Dothan. And went Joseph after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
pieces: "They have left here," the man said. "I heard them say, 'Let us go on to Dothan.'" So Joseph followed his brothers and caught up with them at Dothan.

L.17: And the man said, "They have moved on from here, for I heard [them] saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

R.17: The man said, "They left this place. I heard them say, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

decisions.choice: Dothan: a town on the trade route to Egypt
decisions.reason: Dothan lay about 15 miles (24 km) north of Shechem, near the road that ran from Gilead down to the coast and on to Egypt, which explains the caravan in verse 25.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּבְטֶ֨רֶם֙ יִקְרַ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽתְנַכְּל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they saw him from a distance, and before he drew near to them, and they plotted against him to kill him.
pieces: They spotted him while he was still far off, and before he reached them they schemed to put him to death.

L.18: And they saw him from afar, and before he came near to them they plotted against him to kill him.

R.18: The brothers saw Joseph coming from far away. Before he got to them, they made a plan to kill him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו הִנֵּ֗ה בַּ֛עַל הַחֲלֹמ֥וֹת הַלָּזֶ֖ה בָּֽא׃
records.gloss: And they said each to his brother, behold, [the] master of the dreams, this [one], is coming.
pieces: "Here comes the great dreamer," they said to one another.

L.19: And they said to one another, "Look, this master of dreams is coming.

R.19: They said to each other, "Look, here comes the dreamer!

decisions.choice: master of dreams: a mocking title
decisions.reason: "Master (ba'al) of dreams" means one who specializes in dreams. The brothers use it with contempt.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת וְאָמַ֕רְנוּ חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ וְנִרְאֶ֕ה מַה־יִּהְי֖וּ חֲלֹמֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And now come, and let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say, an animal, wild, has eaten him; and we will see what will be his dreams.
pieces: "Come on, let us kill him now and toss him into one of these cisterns. We can say a wild beast ate him. Then we will find out what comes of his dreams!"

L.20: Now come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits; and we will say, 'A wild animal has devoured him.' And we will see what will become of his dreams."

R.20: Come on, let us kill him and throw his body into one of these empty wells. We can say that a wild animal ate him. Then we will see what happens to his dreams!"

decisions.choice: the pits: cisterns cut in the rock
decisions.reason: A bor was a pit dug to catch rainwater, usually bottle-shaped, so that a person thrown in could not climb out. In the dry season it might be empty (verse 24).

decisions.choice: empty wells
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word; verse 24 says the pit was empty.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיַּצִּלֵ֖הוּ מִיָּדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נַכֶּ֖נּוּ נָֽפֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And heard Reuben and rescued him from their hand and said, let us not strike him [as to] life.
pieces: When Reuben heard this, he tried to save Joseph from them. "We must not kill him," he said.

L.21: And Reuben heard [it] and rescued him from their hand and said, "Let us not take his life."

R.21: But Reuben heard what they said, and he tried to save Joseph from them. He said, "Let us not kill him."

decisions.choice: rescued him: Reuben set out to save him
decisions.reason: The verb states the result Reuben aimed at; verse 22 shows that his plan was to come back later and take Joseph home.

decisions.choice: strike him as to life: kill him
decisions.reason: To strike someone "in the life (nefesh)" is to kill.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֣ם׀רְאוּבֵן֮ אַל־תִּשְׁפְּכוּ־דָם֒ הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל־תִּשְׁלְחוּ־ב֑וֹ לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל־אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said to them Reuben, do not shed blood; throw him into this pit which [is] in the wilderness, and a hand do not stretch out on him, so as to rescue him from their hand, to restore him to his father.
pieces: "Do not shed his blood," Reuben told them. "Throw him into this cistern out here in the wild, but do not lay a hand on him." He meant to rescue him from them and take him back to his father.

L.22: And Reuben said to them, "Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit here in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him." He said this so that he might rescue him from their hand and bring him back to his father.

R.22: "Do not spill his blood," Reuben told them. "Just throw him into this well here in the desert. But do not hurt him." Reuben planned to save Joseph and take him back to his father.

decisions.choice: so as to rescue him: the narrator tells Reuben's hidden purpose
decisions.reason: The last part of the verse is not spoken aloud; it explains why Reuben proposed the pit. As the oldest son, he would answer to Jacob for the boy.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֕י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־אֶחָ֑יו וַיַּפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתּ֔וֹ אֶת־כְּתֹ֥נֶת הַפַּסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was, when came Joseph to his brothers, and they stripped Joseph [of] his tunic, [the] tunic of the palms which [was] on him,
pieces: So when Joseph reached his brothers, they tore off his robe, the long-sleeved robe he was wearing,

L.23: And it happened, when Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles] that [was] on him,

R.23: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his robe, the special robe with long sleeves that he was wearing.

decisions.choice: his tunic, the long tunic: the sign of favor is the first thing taken
decisions.reason: The narrator names the robe twice. Clothing marks each turn in Joseph's story: this robe, the garment left with Potiphar's wife (39:12), and the fine linen Pharaoh gives him (41:42).

records.source: וַיִּ֨קָּחֻ֔הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ הַבֹּ֑רָה וְהַבּ֣וֹר רֵ֔ק אֵ֥ין בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: and they took him and threw him into the pit; and the pit [was] empty, there [was] not in it water.
pieces: and they grabbed him and threw him into the cistern. The cistern was empty; it had no water in it.

L.24: and they took him and threw him into the pit. And the pit [was] empty; [there was] no water in it.

R.24: They grabbed him and threw him into the well. The well was empty. There was no water in it.

records.source: וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֮ לֶֽאֱכָל־לֶחֶם֒ וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְא֔וּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֹרְחַ֣ת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים בָּאָ֖ה מִגִּלְעָ֑ד וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֣ם נֹֽשְׂאִ֗ים נְכֹאת֙ וּצְרִ֣י וָלֹ֔ט הוֹלְכִ֖ים לְהוֹרִ֥יד מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: And they sat down to eat bread, and they lifted their eyes and saw, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites [was] coming from Gilead, and their camels [were] carrying spice and balm and myrrh, traveling to take [them] down to Egypt.
pieces: Then they sat down to their meal. Looking up, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, their camels loaded with gum, balm and resin, which they were taking down to Egypt.

L.25: And they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and look, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying gum, balm and myrrh, on their way to take [it] down to Egypt.

R.25: Then the brothers sat down to eat. They looked up and saw a group of Ishmaelite traders coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices and sweet-smelling gums to sell in Egypt.

decisions.choice: gum, balm and myrrh: costly plant resins
decisions.reason: These were aromatic resins, prized for perfume and medicine and shipped to Egypt, which used them widely, including in embalming. Gilead, east of the Jordan, was famous for its balm (Jeremiah 8:22). The exact plants are uncertain; lot was probably resin from the rockrose (cistus).

decisions.choice: they sat down to eat: callous indifference
decisions.reason: The brothers eat while Joseph is in the pit. Later they recall that they heard his cries for mercy and would not listen (42:21).

decisions.choice: a group of Ishmaelite traders
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a caravan was.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־אֶחָ֑יו מַה־בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י נַהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־אָחִ֔ינוּ וְכִסִּ֖ינוּ אֶת־דָּמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Judah to his brothers, what profit [is it] that we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
pieces: Judah said to his brothers, "What do we gain by killing our brother and hiding the blood?

L.26: And Judah said to his brothers, "What profit [is it] if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

R.26: Judah said to his brothers, "What good will it do us if we kill our brother and hide what we did?

decisions.choice: conceal his blood: hide a murder
decisions.reason: Spilled blood was thought to cry out from the ground (4:10); covering it was an attempt to hide the crime (Job 16:18). Judah's argument is about profit, not mercy.

records.source: לְכ֞וּ וְנִמְכְּרֶ֣נּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים וְיָדֵ֨נוּ֙ אַל־תְּהִי־ב֔וֹ כִּֽי־אָחִ֥ינוּ בְשָׂרֵ֖נוּ ה֑וּא וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶחָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and our hand, let it not be on him, for our brother, our flesh [is] he. And listened his brothers.
pieces: Let us sell him to the Ishmaelites instead and keep our own hands off him. After all, he is our brother, our own flesh and blood." His brothers agreed.

L.27: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be on him, for he [is] our brother, our own flesh." And his brothers listened.

R.27: Let us sell him to these Ishmaelites. Then we will not have to hurt him ourselves. After all, he is our brother and part of our own family." The other brothers agreed.

decisions.choice: our flesh: our own close kin
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means family (29:14). Judah appeals to kinship while proposing to sell his brother as a slave.

records.source: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִן־הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: And passed by men, Midianite[s], traders, and they drew and brought up Joseph from the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty [shekels of] silver; and they brought Joseph to Egypt.
pieces: When the Midianite traders came by, they pulled Joseph up out of the cistern and sold him to the Ishmaelites for {{units:about 8 ounces of silver|twenty shekels of silver}}, and they took Joseph away to Egypt.

L.28: And Midianite men, traders, passed by, and they drew up Joseph and lifted him out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty [shekels of] silver. And they took Joseph to Egypt.

R.28: When the Midianite traders came by, Joseph was pulled up out of the well and sold to the Ishmaelites for {{units:about 8 ounces of silver|twenty shekels of silver}}. Then the traders took Joseph to Egypt.

decisions.choice: Midianites ... Ishmaelites: who pulled Joseph out and who sold him
alternatives: the Midianites pulled him out and sold him to the Ishmaelites, without the brothers
the brothers pulled him out and sold him to the Ishmaelites
decisions.reason: The subject of "drew" and "sold" is not stated. Read with verse 27, the brothers sell him; read on its own, the Midianites do it. "Ishmaelites" and "Midianites" may be overlapping names for the same desert traders (Judges 8:22-24 calls Midianites Ishmaelites), and Joseph himself later says to his brothers, "you sold me" (45:4). Reuben's surprise (verse 29) shows he was not there.

decisions.choice: twenty shekels of silver: the price of a young slave
decisions.reason: "Shekels" is understood. A shekel was a weight, about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams). Twenty shekels is the value set for a boy of five to twenty years in Leviticus 27:5.

decisions.choice: about 8 ounces of silver; with the Measures setting, twenty shekels of silver
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern weight by default and the original unit as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps the Hebrew "twenty [shekels of] silver".

decisions.choice: Joseph was pulled up ... and sold
alternatives: they pulled Joseph up ... and sold him
decisions.reason: Readable uses the passive to keep the Hebrew's unstated subject open.

records.source: וַיָּ֤שָׁב רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל־הַבּ֔וֹר וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵין־יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבּ֑וֹר וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And returned Reuben to the pit, and behold, not Joseph [was] in the pit; and he tore his clothes.
pieces: When Reuben came back to the cistern and saw that Joseph was gone, he tore his clothes in grief.

L.29: And Reuben returned to the pit, and look, Joseph [was] not in the pit; and he tore his clothes.

R.29: Later Reuben went back to the well, and Joseph was not there! Reuben tore his clothes because he was so upset.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes: a sign of grief and alarm
decisions.reason: Tearing one's garments was the customary gesture of mourning or distress (verse 34; 44:13).

decisions.choice: in grief / because he was so upset
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what the gesture meant.

records.source: וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַיֶּ֣לֶד אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וַאֲנִ֖י אָ֥נָה אֲנִי־בָֽא׃
records.gloss: And he returned to his brothers and said, the boy, he is not; and I, where [am] I going?
pieces: He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! And I, what am I going to do?"

L.30: And he returned to his brothers and said, "The boy is not [there]! And I, where shall I go?"

R.30: He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! What am I going to do now?"

decisions.choice: where am I going?: what shall I do, how can I face my father?
decisions.reason: A cry of helplessness. As the firstborn, Reuben would have to answer to Jacob.

records.source: וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־כְּתֹ֣נֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And they took [the] tunic of Joseph, and they slaughtered a male goat of goats and dipped the tunic in the blood.
pieces: They took Joseph's robe, killed a young goat, and soaked the robe in its blood.

L.31: And they took Joseph's tunic and slaughtered a male goat and dipped the tunic in the blood.

R.31: Then the brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's robe in its blood.

decisions.choice: a goat: the deceiver deceived
decisions.reason: Jacob once deceived his own father using a young goat and his brother's clothes (27:9, 15-16). Now his sons deceive him with a goat and Joseph's robe. A young goat appears again in Judah's story (38:17).

records.source: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־כְּתֹ֣נֶת הַפַּסִּ֗ים וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל־אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר־נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם־לֹֽא׃
records.gloss: And they sent [the] tunic of the palms and brought [it] to their father and said, this we have found; examine, please, [whether] the tunic of your son it [is], or not.
pieces: They sent the long-sleeved robe to their father with the message, "We found this. Look it over and see whether it is your son's robe or not."

L.32: And they sent the tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles], and they brought [it] to their father and said, "This we have found. Please examine [it, whether] it [is] your son's tunic or not."

R.32: They sent the special robe to their father and said, "We found this. Look at it carefully. Does it belong to your son?"

decisions.choice: examine, please (hakker-na): look closely and identify
decisions.reason: The same words return in 38:25, when Tamar asks Judah to identify his own seal and staff. Judah, who deceived his father with the words "examine, please", will be confronted with them.

records.source: וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And he recognized it and said, [the] tunic of my son; an animal, wild, has eaten him; surely torn to pieces is Joseph.
pieces: He knew it at once. "It is my son's robe!" he cried. "Some wild animal has eaten him. Joseph has been torn apart, there is no doubt of it!"

L.33: And he recognized it and said, "[It is] my son's tunic! A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!"

R.33: Jacob knew the robe. He said, "It is my son's robe! A wild animal must have eaten him. Joseph has been torn to pieces!"

decisions.choice: surely torn to pieces: the verb doubled in grief
decisions.reason: The doubled verb expresses certainty and anguish. Jacob reaches the conclusion his sons intended without their saying it (verse 20).

records.source: וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל־בְּנ֖וֹ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And tore Jacob his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.
pieces: Jacob tore his clothes, wrapped sackcloth around his waist, and grieved for his son a long time.

L.34: And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.

R.34: Jacob tore his clothes and put on rough cloth to show his sadness. He mourned for his son for a long time.

decisions.choice: sackcloth on his loins: rough goat-hair cloth worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth, coarse cloth usually of goat hair, was tied around the waist as a sign of grief or repentance.

decisions.choice: rough cloth to show his sadness
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom rather than naming the cloth.

records.source: וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל־בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל־בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּֽי־אֵרֵ֧ד אֶל־בְּנִ֛י אָבֵ֖ל שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ אֹת֖וֹ אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And arose all his sons and all his daughters to comfort him, and he refused to be comforted and said, for I will go down to my son mourning to Sheol. And wept for him his father.
pieces: All his sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he would not be consoled. "No," he said, "I will go down to the grave still mourning for my son." And so his father wept for him.

L.35: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, "No, I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol." Thus his father wept for him.

R.35: All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but Jacob would not let them. He said, "I will still be sad for my son when I die and go to be with him in the grave." So Jacob kept crying for Joseph.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place where all the dead go down, good and bad alike, pictured as deep beneath the earth. It is not a place of punishment in Genesis. Jacob means he will grieve until he dies (42:38; 44:29, 31).

decisions.choice: all his daughters: the women of the family
decisions.reason: Only one daughter, Dinah, has been named (30:21). "Daughters" may include daughters-in-law, or there may have been other daughters (46:7).

decisions.choice: his father: Jacob, rather than Isaac
decisions.reason: "His father" most naturally means Joseph's father, Jacob. Isaac's death is reported in 35:29, though the events may overlap in time.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name Sheol; Balanced and Readable say "the grave", the plain sense here.

records.source: וְהַ֨מְּדָנִ֔ים מָכְר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפֽוֹטִיפַר֙ סְרִ֣יס פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׂ֖ר הַטַּבָּחִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And the Medanites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, [the] commander of the bodyguards.
pieces: Meanwhile the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the commander of his guard.

L.36: And the Medanites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard.

R.36: Meanwhile, in Egypt, the traders sold Joseph to Potiphar. Potiphar was one of Pharaoh's officials and the leader of the palace guard.

decisions.choice: Medanites (the Hebrew text) or Midianites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text spells the name Medanites here; the Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient translations have Midianites, as in verse 28. Medan and Midian were both sons of Abraham by Keturah (25:2), and the names may refer to the same group or be a variant spelling.

decisions.choice: an official (saris)
decisions.reason: Saris later came to mean a eunuch, but it is also a general title for a high royal officer, and Potiphar has a wife (39:7). Here it means an official.

decisions.choice: commander of the guard: literally "of the slaughterers"
decisions.reason: Tabbachim can mean butchers or cooks, but here it denotes the royal bodyguard, who also carried out executions; the commander had a prison in his house (40:3).

decisions.choice: the Midianites
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the spelling of verse 28 so the reader does not think a third group is meant; the footnote gives the Hebrew spelling.

decisions.choice: the traders
decisions.reason: Readable avoids a confusing new name.
